When we got back to the pier, passengers were gathering: drovers with their dogs — ancient women in scarlet plaids and white caps, going on to Balmacara or Kyle — a sailor, fresh from China, dressed in his best clothes, with a slate coloured parrot in a wicker cage, which he was conveying to some young people at Broadford.

There stood a ruined sheepfold, and in the corner of two walls some plaids had been stretched to make a tent.

The only building in sight, except the Chapel, in this part of the glen, was a low black hut on the other side of the road, provided for the comfort of the parishioners on wet days ; but on this occasion the people were standing in groups, under the fair canopy of Heaven, the men in their plaids, blue bonnets and kilts, and the old women in bright red cloaks, and snowy white mutches.
